subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is '**either**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes the conditions under which Ari, the pigeon, would join the walks. The correct word should be used to express one of the two conditions: either being carried or walking behind.
 
• "**Either**" is the correct choice as it indicates one of two possibilities or choices, in this case, being carried or walking behind.
 
• Other options ("neither," "never," "ever") are incorrect. "Neither" would imply the impossibility of both actions, which does not match the context. "Never" or "ever" do not convey the idea of choosing between two conditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to fly if he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. He would even try to come on walks with us. This, however, we had to stop for either__ you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own pace to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with exertion.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "Neither" would imply that neither condition is acceptable, which is not the intended meaning.
 
• "Never" means not at any time, which is incorrect because the passage discusses two specific options that are allowed.
 
• "Ever" implies at any time, which doesn't fit the context of the sentence, as "either" is more appropriate for choosing between two alternatives.
